author: Motive (brief 010 A, 2026-10-15)
rule: The rules a generated person must obey. Anything not in this file is rejected (GDD §01 house rules: unknown = reject). Every entry cites its GDD § in `src`; an entry the GDD does not state is marked `proposed: true` with a `reason`, for Sky to accept or strike. Tags in src: [B] built, [S] starting value to tune by playtest.

person.src: §04 person = routine + need + temperament + memory; §09 people checked for one clear need; §09 history, not backstory
person.reason: memory starts empty: a person's history is what the systems record from the first run on (§09), never written backstory. Ties are the only relationships a person starts with.

background.src: life.json generator.tiers: walk, run and cheer only
background.reason: background people carry no name, temperament, need or ties, so the checker can reject a background person that has any; they cannot be approached, questioned or tied to.

bravery.src: §04 bravery [S]: Informant → Helper → Accomplice → Fighter, +1 step per job completed unexposed

resentment.src: §04 resentment [S]: Compliant → Resentful → Informer, +1 step per pressure or exposure

fear.src: §04 talker test names fear; §04 Pressure leaves fear; §05 a threat adds fear
fear.reason: the GDD names fear but gives it no scale. 0–3 integers, one step per pressure or threat, so it weighs against bravery's four steps in the Talker test.

loyalty.src: §04 talker test names loyalty; §04 standing: Hero turning is slower, dearer, loyal
loyalty.reason: the GDD does not say loyal to whom. In the Talker test it must be loyalty to the cell: read as loyalty to an institution, the Office's loyal guard would shield the cell from investigators. Institution loyalty is the Loyal temperament's `institution`, not this number. Every person starts at 0; only being turned raises it.

idealist.name: Idealist
idealist.src: §04 temperament [S]: Idealist responds to Help, refuses bribes
idealist.reason: starting bravery 1 (Helper) is new: §04 says an Idealist volunteers and grows brave fast, so an Idealist begins one step up the ladder. Resentment 0 = Compliant (§04).

mercenary.name: Mercenary
mercenary.menace: discount; sells you to highest bidder
mercenary.src: §04 temperament [S]: Mercenary responds to Pay; ladders start at Informant and Compliant (§04)

fearful.name: Fearful
fearful.reason: starting fear 1 is new: it makes a Fearful person a Talker from the start (1 + 0 > 0 + 0) until Help or a job makes them braver, which is what Fearful means under questioning (§05).

loyal.name: Loyal (institution)
loyal.src: §04 temperament [S]: Loyal (institution) responds to trust over time; reports any approach

institutions.rule: a Loyal person names one institution: a worker is loyal to their employer (work unit or civic employer); a person with no work in the district is loyal to the civic order
institutions.src: §04 Loyal (institution); §01 world: the city fears disorder most, an orderly city runs on routine and paperwork
institutions.reason: the GDD names the temperament but not which institutions exist. Two kinds keep it checkable from data the expander already has (work unit, home).

pressure.leaves: fear; resentment grows; can identify Fixer

approaches.src: §04 approaches [B], Inez's prices in the training mission. Reference prices: a person's own price is Keel's rule, not this file's.

needs.rule: exactly one need per simulated person, from this closed list. `metBy` = the approaches that act on the need (Help meets it, Pressure leans on it, Pay meets it only where money is the need). Pay as a plain bribe and Ask stay open to anyone; they need no need known.

debt.src: §04 Help (clear debt); §07 Inez, café waitress, in debt

housing.src: §07 brief: Vale signed the clearance order for the marked block
housing.reason: a home under a clearance order or a waiting list: the Handover's own cause, and a need only the civic order can meet or threaten. Needs a home in the district.

papers.src: §01 world: records are physical (microfilm, punch cards, stamped forms)
papers.reason: a permit, licence or record on file that must be stamped, found or lost. The world's records are paper held by people, so a clerk can meet it and a threat can file one.

kin.src: §04 between missions: arrested (lost unless freed); standing: Hero frees arrested locals
kin.reason: a family member arrested or in trouble. Needs a family tie, so the checker can see whose kin it is.

care.src: §08 wounds: a turned doctor heals fast and quietly
care.reason: illness at home, met by a doctor contact. Help only: §06 content line keeps harm to bystanders out of leverage.

protection.reason: someone leans on them. Needs a rival tie, so the threat is a person in the cast, not prose.

advancement.reason: wants the better post or the access that comes with it. A promotion is a §04 outcome, so a person who wants one gives Help a lasting payoff. Needs work in the district.

secret.reason: something they hide, learned by Listen. Gives Pressure a target that is not money, and Help (keeping it buried) a quieter answer.

requiresKinds.home: a home plot in the district (commuters and visitors from beyond the sheet have none)
requiresKinds.work: a work unit or civic employer in the district

family.src: §04 between missions: introduces a friend (new contact); arrested (lost unless freed)
family.reason: limit 4 [S]. Family may live apart and need not share a family name (a mixed cast, §15).

workmate.src: §08 assets: Inez introduces café contacts; Act II takes a workplace
workmate.reason: limit 3 [S]. Both work the same unit or the same civic employer, so a workplace can be turned link by link (§08).

regular.src: §08 economy: café owner tips needs before Scout listens; §05 counters: reach witness first
regular.reason: a customer who comes back. The customer's routine stops at the other person's work unit, so the tie is checkable on the routine. 3 out, 12 in [S]: staff know many regulars.

debtor.reason: who owes whom. 2 owed, 6 owing in [S]. A debt need may be owed to a bureau or pawnbroker as a trade, so a debt need does not require a debtor tie.

rival.src: §04 Mercenary sells you to highest bidder; §05 rivals
rival.reason: one rival at most [S], in the same trade in the district or at the same employer: a grudge with a place.

betweenKinds.same-employer: both work the same unit or the same civic employer
betweenKinds.routine-stop: the from-person's routine has a stop at the to-person's work unit while they are on shift
betweenKinds.same-trade-or-employer: same occupation anywhere in the district, or the same employer

ties.src: §09 people: occupation × temperament × need × relationships × routine
ties.reason: 1–8 ties per simulated person [S]: nobody stands alone (introductions, §04, need someone to introduce), nobody is a hub. Ties join simulated people only; background people have none.

talker.src: §04 talker [S]: questioned, a person gives up known facts if fear + resentment > bravery + loyalty (deterministic). Facts: saw Fixer's face, knows cell car, saw where/when

lie.src: §04 brave helped contact lies → nothing or false lead; §05 Hero campaign: brave locals give false leads
lie.reason: the GDD says brave and helped; brave is read as bravery ≥ 1 (Helper). Which of nothing or a false lead is decided by the district's standing, so it stays deterministic.

positions.rule: every work unit has exactly one keeper; the rest of its staff take the other positions of its category. A mission casts by position and place (a server on shift at the café), never by name.
positions.src: brief 010 Fixed: mission people are city people pinned by role; §08 café owner tips needs; §07 cast (café waitress)
positions.reason: the Handover must cast a waitress (server), and §08 a café owner (keeper). The categories are life.json's; the positions within them are new.

temperamentsBy.rule: a person's temperament must be one its occupation (trade) or role allows. Every trade and role allows at least two, so no job reads as one kind of person (§09 risk: sameness).

pawnbroker.reason: a creditor: debt is the need the Handover turns on (§07). An Idealist lender forgives it, so the city's creditors are never Idealist.

credit-bureau.reason: as pawnbroker: the city's creditors are never Idealist (§07 debt).

temperamentsBy.tradesSrc: the 39 trades of plan standards.frontage.trades = the 39 occupations of life.json generator.occupations (category from life.json); all four temperaments unless marked: §04 Hero and Menace turn different halves of the city, so most jobs carry every kind

visitor.src: life.json routines shopper, reveller; commuters from beyond the sheet
visitor.reason: a simulated person who neither lives nor works in the district (shopper, reveller) still needs a role the checker knows.

docker.src: life.json routines.docker; §08 Act II takes a workplace e.g. docks
docker.reason: port workers hired by shift at the hiring hall are not its staff, so they need their own role.

clerk.src: §08 economy: clerk skims cash; life.json civicEmployers records-office
clerk.reason: the Records Office's staff. All four: §08's skimming clerk is a Mercenary, and the Office must hold some who can be helped.

guard.src: §05 security: guard on door routine (café stop pre-shift); §07 cast; brief 010 A (Sky): Loyal to the Office or Mercenary, never Idealist
guard.reason: Sky's question in the brief, answered yes. Not Fearful either: a guard who folds to a threat would make §07 route A's Help-and-call the costly way round.

official-driver.reason: all four: the Handover picks a driver it can turn (brief 010 D), the city does not shape its drivers for one mission.

councillor.src: §07 Councillor Vale signed the clearance order
councillor.reason: the one who signs clearance orders. Never Idealist, for the same reason creditors are not: the order is the harm.

watcher.src: §01 world: cameras are closed-circuit, watched by people; §05 watchers
watcher.reason: the people behind the cameras. Never Idealist: a watcher's log is the city's record against the cell (§05).

patrol-officer.src: §05 security: patrol sweep, response unit; §06 health guard/officer 3

investigator.reason: as guard: Loyal or Mercenary. An investigator who could be helped across would undo §05's pressure.

cafe.src: civic-block.json cafe (Corner café); plan standards.frontage.placement.corner: corners on two streets take an anchor trade (w ≥ 18), else a diner; the records mix lists diner
cafe.reason: the café is none of the 39 trades by name. A 22 m corner unit takes a diner (the plan's corner rule; diner is an anchor in the records mix and opens 6–24, covering the 17:00 Handover). Datum or Vantage may name it otherwise.

civic.reason: the city's own security, which the plan does not site. Its people are loyal to the civic order (institution kind civic).

names.pool: one pool per district, carried by the cast tables (brief 010 B); every simulated person's given and family name come from it
names.noEraDate: no digits, years, dates, generational suffixes (Jr, Sr, II, III) or titles in a name; the pattern forbids them
names.src: §15 people: people prompts carry no era date; mixed cast (ages, builds, ethnicities); brief 010 A: a pool per district, no era date, a mixed cast
names.reason: the GDD gives the principle, not the numbers. Each pool entry is tagged with one origin from the closed list; ≥ 6 origins and no origin over a quarter of a pool make a mixed cast checkable. 60 × 80 = 4,800 full names keeps every simulated person in a district unique. The avoid list holds names that date a person to 1950s Americana (the §15 failure in names). Pinned: the GDD names Inez and Vale, so the person the Handover pins by role takes that name part; no other name is ever authored.
